sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's accelerating digital payments and fintech adoption is structurally lifting local tech platforms like ELIT and ASGR, decoupling them from US rate sensitivity.
Domestic tech valuations remain attractive versus US peers, with ID tech outperforming by 2.27pp today, signaling persistent local capital rotation into high-growth names.
US mega-cap tech (AMZN, NOW) faces margin compression from AI capex and regulatory overhang, making ID-listed tech a lower-risk growth proxy for regional investors.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names on local strength (ELIT, ASGR) while trimming US mega-cap exposure (AMZN, NOW) into the -1.78% US drag; the WATCH signal favors rotation into domestic digital infrastructure and e-commerce enablers, not broad beta. Prioritize ELIT and ASGR for momentum, avoid YELO/SLIS until volume confirms.

US financials' slight drag is noise; stay overweight Indonesia financials for the next quarter.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Coal equities are re-rating on resilient thermal demand and tight Indonesian supply, favoring low-cost producers like ADRO and MBAP with export flexibility.
Nickel and downstream processing names (INPS, AADI) benefit from EV battery demand and government-backed smelter expansions, despite global price volatility.
Energy service and infrastructure plays (SLB, BAJA) are gaining from upstream capex recovery, but gains are selective and require earnings delivery to sustain.
sectors.ai: Buy MBAP on its 24.8% surge, but treat as momentum—lock partial profits and trail stops; rotate into ADRO for coal cash-flow resilience and INPS for nickel upside. Sector breadth is positive but not euphoric, so add on dips rather than chase. Trim ALKA and BAJA into strength, as their moves lack volume confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's 2025-2034 RUPTL accelerates solar and geothermal capacity additions, creating durable order flow for domestic EPC and IPP players like LAPD and PGEO.
Carbon trading under the Bursa Karbon Indonesia is monetizing emissions reductions, structurally lifting margins for early movers such as ESSA and POWR.
US climate-tech selloff is idiosyncratic to IRA policy uncertainty, not a read-through to Indonesia's state-backed energy transition, which remains insulated from US politics.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesia renewables leaders (LAPD, ESSA, POWR) on policy tailwinds from the new RUPTL and carbon trading; US weakness is noise. Rotate into geothermal (PGEO) and water (AWK) for defensive yield, but trim GGRP on valuation.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's FMCG sector benefits from resilient domestic consumption as BI holds rates, supporting staple demand despite global volatility.
Commodity-linked consumer names (OILS, AGAR) are gaining structural traction from palm oil and agri-export pricing power, a durable margin driver.
Micro-cap momentum (BIKE, SSTM) reflects retail speculation, but liquidity risk is high; institutional flows favor mid-cap staples with dividend yields.
sectors.ai: Buy BIKE and SSTM on momentum but rotate profits into OILS and AGAR for sustained earnings; consumer staples remain defensive amid BI's rate pause, so overweight names with export or commodity linkage. Trim CRSN and HADE into strength as retail sentiment fades.
